chunks: How [will it be] when a calamity strikes them for what their hands have sent forth before, then they come to you swearing by God, 'We intended nothing but good and success.'

key_terms.بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ: for what their hands have sent forth (deeds)
key_terms.تَوْفِيقًا: success or finding the right path

ai.seo_question: What do the hypocrites claim when calamity strikes them despite their misdeeds?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (4:106) is often linked to the hypocrites (Munafiqun) who, after being struck by divine punishment for their hidden treachery, rushed to the Prophet Muhammad to swear oaths of sincerity. It underscores the psychological state of those whose external compliance masks internal corruption, highlighting how calamity serves as a catalyst for their performative repentance rather than genuine spiritual transformation.
